original_card.question: Which unresolved physical correction, endpoint transport or hosting obligation in a pinned P104 follow-up can be closed or decisively rejected?
methods: Construct one side-correction word at an explicit chronological cut with the needed frames still available.
Derive a lower bound on the side correction and hosting costs that decides whether this channel can beat the selected budget.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An exact arbitrary-input identity, source/target frame availability and restoration at the chosen cut, plus the complete channel+correction+idle/hosting bill or an explicit favorable bound. The native channel alone is not a supplier. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the P104 row in research-family-status.md and its exact pending source heads before choosing a task. #1991 is the reviewed channel; #2586 is a pending physical dual with explicit added transport costs, not an admitted supplier.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only. Read the named package and review before relying on its local evidence; this command is not its replay or supplier admission.

original_card.first_experiment: Check live claims, pin the chosen follow-up and reproduce only the evidence needed for one unresolved obligation. Compare its complete correction/transport/hosting invoice with the target budget; test legal chronological access. Do not rebuild #1991 or assume #2586 has solved global admission.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Completing an already realized changed channel tests a concrete construction opportunity, instead of refining the incumbent packing. A positive local result still needs global and all-size admission.
allowed_variations: One correction factorization, one chronological cut, or one explicit hosting obstruction.
A changed correction schedule with an updated full bill and native frame contract.
scope_change_triggers: Recompiling the already certified low-rank channel without closing a new obligation.
Treating a pending ancestor, local histogram or unpriced side correction as an admitted global supplier.
Repeating a correction or physical conversion already supplied by a pending follow-up without adding independent coverage or a different unresolved obligation.

actual_scope: For the all-104-target P104 X-only I-G/2 correction on the frozen PR1972/PR1991 paths (published relay-checker grammar G, i.e. its part-B replay rules and completion conditions, and a widened grammar G' with singular in-frame mixing): price a rank-one-rectangle mixer design (invertible mixing of rank-one block values at shared frames) against the PR2675 fixed-template ideal-idle screen at the selected complex saving (window L about 387-482), build only if a named path exists, and otherwise prove a top-level lower bound on new helper lifetimes.
scope_change_reason: The card asks which P104 correction/transport/hosting obligation can be closed or decisively rejected. This work narrows it to the helper-lifetime count of the X-only correction route of #2245, the term separating the passing 208-lifetime relaxation from the 1031-lifetime relay-v2 construction. Pricing came first and no complete design could be priced into the window, so the single pivot was a lower bound rather than a construction. The result is scoped: floors 219/234 (216/234 with singular in-frame mixing) lie inside (208, 482] and neither close nor reject the route. It does not concern #2586's nonmonotone physical inverse-transpose or the #2741 pair consumer.
bottleneck_link: P104 completion is a revision-5 lead. On the X-only monotone correction route of #2245, screened by the PR2675 fixed template and the window bill, the correction must fit in at most 482 new helper lifetimes with a passing profile before hosting, native, dual and precision obligations matter. To our knowledge (after an overlap search, which is not proof of novelty) this package gives the first all-target, all-shape lifetime floors above 208 with a written proof in the relay-permitting model; relay-v2's unproved same-model sharing-count estimate L >~ 387 is stronger. It also pins the exact top-level obstruction to lossless multi-value carriage. Because that obstruction uses only a small part of the slack, further constructions or floors on this route should target gathering below the 7-dimensional frames. The floors say nothing about #2586's physical inverse-transpose or the PR2458+PR2712 pair consumer rejected by #2741.
stop_rule: Price first: build no word and run no search unless a priced complete mixer design has a named path into L about 387-482 passing the PR2675 fixed template at saving 0.0016754627 (it did not). Then one pivot: a single top-level lower-bound attempt (bound in (208, 482] = scoped note; above 482 = decisive; none above 208 within about 60 min = handoff only). No kappa claims; one 60-minute extension recorded.
evidence: Written proof (PROOF.md: Lemmas 1-4 and 4', the counting theorem with closed form E >= ceil(A/4)) over finite facts F1-F8 and F7'-F8'. Every finite fact is recomputed by two separately written exact standard-library implementations (verify.py/top_primary.py with echelon frames; independent.py with point masks, annihilators, E8 inner products, the normal identity, direct search and the closed form), and verify.py requires them to agree key by key. Floors: 219 (G, full model), 234 (final-frame class, G and G'), 216 (G', full model). The necessary 2x2 test T holds for 288/5356 final-frame pairs and 414 full-model pairs (240 good-good, the count with proven meaning); 0 certified targets have two complementary halves passing T (F8), explained structurally by complementary halves always holding 24 + 24 sources while every T-pair has |S(K)| in {18, 20}; T' (singular) holds for 672/1038 pairs, and 12 good targets have two halves in G' (IDs compared by both implementations). Each zero count except the F1 diagonal (which follows from the port norms) has a nonzero same-path companion statistic. Demonstration word (4974 lifetimes, sha256 cf8f444b...) accepted by the unchanged published checker and both replayers; seven negative controls rejected by all three for pinned reasons. Side certificates: geometry lemma max |S||T| = 48 for dims 1-4 (frame BFS with equality counts; subset enumeration for the maximum and shapes) and the frame-class block inventory (primary only). Allowances 333/431/478/482 reproduced with merged ceiling.py. Local runs: CPython 3.14.4; the registered 3.12 replay is left to hosted CI. Author-checked; reviewed only by AI review passes in the same loop; no human or proof-assistant review.

open_questions.question: Can lower-level gathering be charged to give a floor above 482, or to locate a lossless lower structure?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the only remaining way to reject the X-only correction route or to find a design in the 387-482 window; we expect (heuristically, not proved) that top-level reasoning alone cannot exceed 416.
open_questions.first_step: Extend Lemma 4 to 6-frames M inside a perfect half K and pose the per-level excess counting as an exact integer program over the 7- and 6-levels.
open_questions.blocked_by: Case explosion at 6-frames (up to 7 seven-frames and 4 target hyperplanes each); needs a structured relaxation rather than enumeration.

open_questions.question: Do the 20 permissively treated targets (last intermediate frame holding 3 or 12 sources) really escape the tight-target structure?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Treating them exactly could lift the full-model floor from 219 toward 234.
open_questions.first_step: Run Lemmas 3-4 with their actual non-complementary two-covers and lower-dimensional entry frames; the broader F8 check already finds no target with two T-partners whose halves cover R_t, so what is missing is a proof that T is necessary for them.
open_questions.blocked_by: Their covers have exclusive parts spanning only 5-6 dimensions, so entry frames can lie below dimension 7.

open_questions.question: Can a non-tight target a absorb b_a imperfect halves of tight targets, one per lifetime?
open_questions.why_it_matters: All four floor minimisers rely on non-tight targets with b_a = 3 absorbing three halves each. If each non-tight target could absorb at most b_a - 1 halves, the same counting would give L >= 243 in the final-frame class; L >= 260 needs absorption excluded entirely (both conditional values recomputed by both implementations).
open_questions.first_step: Enumerate three-covers of R_t by hyperplanes of H_t and apply the Lemma 4 test with the induced partial constraints.
open_questions.blocked_by: C(255,3) triples per target need bitset pruning.

open_questions.question: Is there a written proof of the geometry lemma |S(F)||T(F)| <= 48 for source-spanned frames of dimension <= 4?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would explain the 1x48 = 2x24 = 4x12 = 6x8 ceiling structurally and might extend to higher dimensions.
open_questions.first_step: Use E8 non-orthogonality of the 104 ports (for s != t, q_s in H_t iff <p_s,p_t> != 0, finite fact F1; q_t is not in H_t).
open_questions.blocked_by: The 104 ports are not a full E8 orbit.

open_questions.question: Do the floors 219/234 survive the free root-code reads of #2383 and the read-only original-helper reads of #2467?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Those PRs keep the 208 floor under these extra reads; if 219/234 also survive, they apply to those wider models. They are not claimed there now.
open_questions.first_step: Check whether any of the 72 original helper paths visits a 7-frame inside a target hyperplane (#2467 shows none visits a target hyperplane itself), then restate Lemmas 3(b) and 4 modulo the root code using #2383's invariant that the source part at frame V lies in the root code plus U(V).
open_questions.blocked_by: Lemma 4's determinant argument uses exact entry supports; with free root-code reads, entry values are known only modulo the root code.

open_questions.question: Should the sharper private-half count be adopted, raising the proved floors to 250 (final-frame class, G and G') and 234 (full model, G)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It uses only finite facts already certified here (pair halves hold at most 24 sources; no T-pair, and no final-frame T'-pair, has |S(K)| = 24; F4). No decision would change (250 < 333).
open_questions.first_step: Write the count as a lemma in PROOF.md section 4 (a private half, lying in no other target hyperplane, can be served only by unshared junk; every perfect half has a private complement) and add the refined minimisation E >= X + tau_A + max(0, ceil((2 tau_B - (X + 2m) - 2(pi - m_p))/2)) to both implementations.
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing known. It was proposed by an AI review pass in this loop's last review round and re-checked only in a scratch computation (cover census, exact minimisation: E >= 42 final-frame, E >= 26 full model in G); it is not in the registered replay. The G' full-model value was not computed because T' admits pairs with |S(K)| = 24 there.
